# Strict Mode, accessibility and end-to-end checks

> Render under `<StrictMode>` to catch missing cleanups; query by role; run axe in Playwright against the production build.

🔴 advanced · React 18.0+ · Testing › Integration testing

**Playground:** `npm run dev` → [`#/entry/testing-strict-mode-and-a11y`](http://localhost:5173/#/entry/testing-strict-mode-and-a11y)

## Concept

Strict Mode mounts, unmounts and remounts components in development, so a missing cleanup shows up as duplicated listeners or registrations. Queries by role and label double as accessibility checks. The Playwright suite (`e2e/`) runs axe on real pages in Chromium.

## Problem

Effects that work once can break on remount, and UI that passes unit tests can still be unusable with a keyboard or screen reader.

- [`src/esp-demo/EspDemo.test.tsx`](../../src/esp-demo/EspDemo.test.tsx)

- [`src/app/App.test.tsx`](../../src/app/App.test.tsx)

## Execution flow

1. Wrap renders in `<StrictMode>` (the esp-js tests do) and assert observable behaviour, not render counts.
2. Prefer `getByRole(name)` / `getByLabelText` queries; they fail when elements lack accessible names.
3. `npm run test:e2e` builds the app, serves it and runs Playwright + `@axe-core/playwright` (serious/critical violations fail).

## Edge cases

- axe in jsdom cannot evaluate colour contrast; the Playwright run in a real browser can.
